title: Cohort-driven A/B framework and dashboards for batching & caching metric contracts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a hypothesis-driven experimentation scaffold and companion dashboards to validate batching + KV-caching configuration recommendations. Goal: safely surface automated config suggestions that reduce per-token cost without causing latency/quality regressions for customer cohorts. This ticket covers metric contract definitions, cohorting logic, statistical tests, synthetic replay wiring, dashboard prototypes, and an automated rollback gate tied to canary rollout automation.
acceptance_criteria: Config change can be deployed to a canary cohort via the rollout controller and reversed automatically if guardrails are tripped
Dashboard shows cohort-level primary/secondary metrics, uplift/delta, and statistical significance for each experiment arm
Metric contracts (primary/secondary/guardrail) are documented and wired to alerts with concrete thresholds
Synthetic replay harness can reproduce baseline vs experiment distributions for two representative workload cohorts
PRs for rollout automation and dashboard merged with unit + integration tests and a runbook for manual rollback
progress_updates: 2025-10-28: Kicked off with PM and Design; agreed to focus on two cohorts (low-latency interactive and high-throughput batch) and a shared eval prompt set for quality checks.
2025-10-30: Prototype Grafana dashboard created (mocked data) showing p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, and model-quality delta for eval prompts.
2025-11-01: Integrated synthetic traffic replayer (traffic-replay service) with staging runtime; confirmed replay can reproduce token distribution and prefix lengths.
2025-11-03: Ran sample-size calculations — estimated 48 hours of production canary at 5% traffic split for medium-volume customers to reach power 0.8 for cost uplift >8%.
2025-11-04: First end-to-end smoke canary executed with a limited set of customers; alerting hooks validated and automatic rollback path exercised in a test namespace.
analysis_notes: Primary metric: cost_per_1k_tokens (unit economics) normalized by request type and model family. Treat as improvement when lower by >5% with p < 0.05.
Latency metrics: p50/p95 RTT and tail error spikes. Any p95 regression >10% or error-rate increase >0.5pp triggers guardrail.
Quality validation: run eval prompt set (n=250 prompts) comparing generation quality using automated BLEU/ROUGE proxies + manual review for cohorts flagged by the harness.
Segmentation: cohort by SLA tier (free/standard/enterprise), request size buckets (short/medium/long), and model family (openchat-*, redwood-*).
Statistical approach: use two-sided permutation tests and bootstrap CIs for non-normal metrics; maintain an experiment-level alpha of 0.05 with sequential correction for multiple arms.
Counterfactual replays: capture request metadata and KV-cache hit shaped traces; replay with and without KV-prefetch to estimate prefetched hit delta and cost impact.
Rollback automation: controller watches metric contract state; if any guardrail tripped for >5 minutes, controller flips config and posts a Slack incident message with links + rollforward checklist.

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3C_experiment-assets -- eval prompt set, manual review notes, chart exports
runbook: Pre-check: validate metric stream freshness and cohort assignment coverage >99%
Start canary: deploy config to 3% traffic for 2 hours, then 10% for 24 hours if no guardrails tripped
Monitor: automated alerts for p95 latency, cost delta, error-rate, and quality regressions; human review if any alert fires
Rollback: controller performs immediate rollback when guardrail satisfied for 5 consecutive minutes and annotates the experiment run
Postmortem: collect traces, sample payloads, and run additional synthetic replays before reattempting changes
notes_for_reviewers: Design trade-offs: we prefer cohorting at the request-router layer to avoid cross-customer noise, but that requires a small router change (see PR link).
Open question: whether to include embedding/semantic-search workloads in first wave — currently scoped out due to different token patterns.
Ops requirement: need an alerting budget for noisy experiments; Ops requested a quiet-hours suppression window for enterprise customers.
